rationale: Ceilings for scripts/check-docs-web-vitals.mjs (#474 WBS-H075). Derived from measurement, not from a target: three full passes over the five pages below, Lighthouse 13.4.1 mobile emulation, against the built apps/docs/dist served with gzip, on an Apple silicon laptop.

largestContentfulPaintMs 1340: the worst of the 15 measurements was 1225 ms (components/table). 1340 is that value plus 115 ms, i.e. 9.4% headroom (1225 x 1.094), rounded to a flat number. The other pages measured 904-1222 ms.

totalBlockingTimeMs 150: measured 0 ms on every page in every pass. A 0 ms ceiling would not be a regression guard but a machine test, because Lighthouse derives TBT from real task durations on the host CPU and a slower machine produces long tasks where this one produced none. 150 ms is the top of Lighthouse's green band for mobile TBT, so anything under it still scores well; anything over it means new blocking script, which is the regression worth catching on a static documentation site.

cumulativeLayoutShift 0.05: measured 0.000 on every page in every pass. Half of Lighthouse's 0.1 'good' threshold, rather than 0.000, because a late font swap can shift layout on a slow load without anything having regressed.
minPerformanceScore 0.95: measured 1.00 on every page in every pass. It is a backstop over the three metrics above, not an independent limit.

The three ceilings are not equally strong, and should not be read as such: only LCP can trip on a normal regression, because only LCP is set close to what was measured (9.4% above 1225 ms). TBT and CLS sit above a measured zero, so their headroom relative to the measurement is unbounded; they catch a change that introduces blocking script or layout shift, not a gradual slide.
